title: fix: Load extensions on HTTP VFS connections, and run the HTTP VFS tests for real
description:
The three tests in `tests/testthat/test-httpvfs.R` that start a local httpuv server have failed on every CI run, `main` included, while `R CMD check` reported `Status: OK`. The testthat summary in the logs reads `[ FAIL 3 | ... ]`, but each test's cleanup then disconnected a fixture connection that was already closed, and testthat only counts a test as errored when the error is its last result (`summarize_one_test_results()`), so the "Already disconnected" warning recorded after the error hid it from `test_check()`. This came up on #829, where the maintainer asked for a fix from `main` that makes such errors fail loudly. This pull request makes those errors fail the check, and then fixes what they were reporting.

**Masking.** The fixture database is built and closed in its own scope (`http_test_db()`), and the remote connection's cleanup is registered with `withr::defer()` only once the connection has opened. An error therefore stays the last result of the test. With only this change, `test_local(stop_on_failure = TRUE)` on the old tests stops with "Test failures."

**Extension loading over the HTTP VFS.** `sqlite3_load_extension()` loads through the connection's VFS, and the HTTP VFS returned NULL from `xDlOpen()`, so `dbConnect()` with the default extensions failed with an empty "Failed to load extension:" message on any remote database. The VFS now delegates `xDlOpen()`, `xDlError()`, `xDlSym()` and `xDlClose()` to the default VFS, as it already does for randomness, sleep and time. The metadata probe also no longer sets `CURLOPT_HEADER`, which made libcurl print the response headers of every remote open to stdout.

**`sqliteRemote()` loads the default extensions.** It passed `default.extensions = FALSE` to `dbConnect()`, a workaround for the bug above. Its connections now load the default extensions as `dbConnect()` does, so functions such as `stdev()` work on remote databases, and callers can pass `default.extensions` themselves. This is a behavior change for `sqliteRemote()` users.

**Timeouts and interrupts.** The VFS set no libcurl limits, so a server that accepted a connection and never answered blocked R, and with it `R CMD check`, indefinitely. Every handle now gives up connecting after `RSQLITE_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 30) and aborts a transfer that receives less than one byte per second for `RSQLITE_HTTP_STALL_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 60); only whole numbers of seconds of at least 1 are honored, in any notation R writes such as `1e+05`; larger values are capped at 2147483 seconds (and libcurl 8.19.0 or later caps the stall timeout at 65535 seconds itself), and anything else uses the default, as documented in `?sqliteHttpConfig`. A handle whose limits cannot be set is not used, and the open then fails with "unable to open database file" (a query with "disk I/O error"). A progress callback aborts the transfer when the user interrupts R, through `R_ToplevelExec()` so that no longjmp crosses SQLite or libcurl; it uses `CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION`, or `CURLOPT_PROGRESSFUNCTION` with libcurl older than 7.32.0. Opening used to probe the server up to four times (the file size and the header read each sent a HEAD and a GET); a failed probe is now not repeated within one open, and a HEAD that cannot connect, times out or is interrupted skips the GET, so a silent server costs one timeout and one Ctrl-C aborts the open. A stall during the open reports "unable to open database file", during a query "disk I/O error".

The server runs in a separate R process started with `callr::r_bg()` (`local_http_server()` in the new `helper-httpvfs.R`): the VFS performs blocking libcurl requests on the main R thread, so an httpuv app in the same process can never answer, and the old tests would have hung once they reached the VFS. The child gets the test's temporary directory as its `TMPDIR`, so the session directory it leaves behind when killed is removed with it, and it logs each request it receives. The test server answers HEAD without a body; httpuv otherwise sends the body for HEAD too, which corrupts the next response on the kept-alive connection and made some runs fail (one in five locally) with libcurl's "HTTP/0.9 not allowed" error. The Range test compares the `range_requests` and `bytes_fetched` counters of `sqliteHttpStats()` with their values before the query, because they are process-wide, checks that the server sent less than the whole file, pads the database so that the query reads only a fraction of it, and calls `stdev()` through `sqliteRemote()`. A new test opens a server that accepts requests and never answers them, with `RSQLITE_HTTP_STALL_TIMEOUT=1`, expects the open to fail within seconds, and checks that the server received exactly one request, the HEAD, so a refused connection cannot pass for a stall. title: fix: Never restart a statement after an error in `dbFetch()` or `dbBind()`
description:
Found while reviewing #795, where the maintainer asked for a separate pull request from `main`: two pre-existing bugs in how a result behaves after an SQLite error. Both come from the same SQLite behavior: since 3.7.0, `sqlite3_step()` on a statement that failed resets it and runs it again from the start instead of returning `SQLITE_MISUSE`, and RSQLite stepped such a statement again on the next fetch.

**Error in the middle of a result.** When `sqlite3_step()` failed after some rows had been returned, `dbFetch()` raised the error, but `dbHasCompleted()` stayed `FALSE` and the next `dbFetch()` restarted the query from the first row. It returned a row of `NA` followed by the first rows again, or raised the same error again, with `dbGetRowCount()` growing each time. This affected plain queries, any parameter set of a `dbBind()` with several sets, and a later parameter set that fails to bind. Now an error ends the execution: `dbHasCompleted()` returns `TRUE`, a further `dbFetch()` returns zero rows with the result's columns, and a new `dbBind()` makes the result usable again. `dbGetRowCount()` no longer counts the rows read by a fetch that fails, also not when the conversion to a data frame fails, because they are not returned.

**Failed `dbBind()`.** When the first parameter set of a list `dbBind()` failed, either in binding or in the statement, its parameters stayed in place. The next `dbFetch()` ran them once more, raising the error again, or returned rows from a statement whose bindings were partly cleared. Now a failed `dbBind()` leaves the result unbound, as it was before the first bind: `dbFetch()` raises "Query needs to be bound before fetching", which is what a failed Arrow bind in #795 already does. `dbHasCompleted()` returns `FALSE` and `dbGetRowCount()` returns 0; `dbGetRowsAffected()` reports the changes since the failed bind, for example 2 when the third of four inserts fails, and 0 for a failed query (it stays `NA` only before the first bind).

**Why these semantics.** DBI's specification does not cover errors during a fetch. Completing the result follows from `dbHasCompleted()` returning `TRUE` "if no more rows are available for fetching" and from fetches past the end returning zero rows; #795 does the same when a later Arrow parameter set fails to bind. The rejected alternative was to keep the error and raise it again on every further `dbFetch()`: that needs extra state, because SQLite's error message is overwritten by later calls, and it turns `while (!dbHasCompleted(res))` loops that handled the error into repeated errors. A failed `dbBind()` is treated differently because the failing call is the bind itself: asking for a new bind is louder than silently returning zero rows that look like an empty result.

**Merging into #795.** The merge conflicts in `src/SqliteResultImpl.cpp`, in `bind()` and `step()`, and in `src/SqliteResultImpl.h`, in the state block. Suggested resolution: in the header, keep #795's `int64_t nrows_` and `executions_` and add this PR's `bool bind_started_` after `ready_` (the constructor and `n_rows_affected()` merge cleanly). Keep #795's `bind()`. In `step()`, keep `arrow_row_read_ = false;` and then this PR's `try`/`catch`. Move the failure handling out of `bind_arrow()`, which then just calls `after_set_params()`, and into `after_set_params()`: set `bind_started_ = true;` next to `total_changes_start_`, and wrap `bind_row()` and `after_bind()` in a `try` whose `catch (...)` resets `params_`, `ready_ = false`, `complete_ = false` and `nrows_ = 0` and then rethrows. #795's `params_.reset(); ready_ = false;` alone is not enough: without the other two resets, `dbHasCompleted()` stays `TRUE` and `dbGetRowCount()` keeps the previous count after a failed bind. In `fetch_arrow_rows()`, drop the `++nrows_` in the loop and add `nrows_ += n;` just before `chunk.move(out)`, so that, as in `fetch_rows()`, rows count only once the chunk is built. With this resolution the whole test suite passes, including `test-arrow.R`, and both binds and both fetch paths behave as described here. No existing test covers the `fetch_arrow_rows()` step, so the merge should add an Arrow counterpart of "an error in the middle of a result completes it" to `test-arrow.R` (a `dbFetchArrowChunk()` whose chunk fails, then `dbGetRowCount()`, `dbHasCompleted()` and an empty next chunk), and carry #795's comment on why a stream that fails on its first row is not kept into `after_set_params()`.

The tests are in `tests/testthat/test-dbSendQuery.R`; all six fail on `main`. A [clean review](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/pull/830#issuecomment-6772663614) found no High or Medium issue; four of its Low findings are fixed up to 88cc2af9, which a [second clean review](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/pull/830#issuecomment-6773298506) confirmed without High or Medium findings, and what remains is listed under [Accepted limitations](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/pull/830#issuecomment-6773306833).
